 Judgment
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 11th sep 2018 passed in MVC No.560 of 2015, the appellant-Reliance General Insurance Company Limited, has preferred this Appeal. .
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. The basic details of the case are as follows:
On the evening of July 10, 2015, at approximately 8:00 pm, the petitioner was traveling as a passenger on a motorcycle with registration number KA-29/U-4991 on Bagalkot-Kaladgi Road.
As they approached a spinning mill, a lorry with registration number KA-29/U-5937 was being driven at a high speed and in a reckless and negligent manner, posing a threat to human life.
This lorry collided with the motorcycle, resulting in the petitioner sustaining severe injuries.
Following the accident, the petitioner was immediately transported to Dr. Katti Hospital in Bagalkot, where he NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB received medical treatment as an inpatient for around 15 days.
Subsequently, he was transferred to Dr. Vijay Kanti Hospital in Bagalkot and then referred to Miraj Hospital.
It is mentioned that the petitioner incurred medical expenses amounting to Rs.3,00,000/- for his treatment.
Furthermore, the petitioner continues to require medical care, and it is estimated that he will need Rs.50,000/- for future medical expenses.

However, due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has become unable to work and has suffered permanent disability.
Consequently, the petitioner is seeking compensation for the damages suffered as a result of the accident.
4. Following the issuance of notice, both respondents 1 and 2 submitted their written statements.
5. Respondent No.1 alleged the petition as false, frivolous, and vexatious.
It was argued that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and disproportionate.

It was asserted that the vehicle in question was insured with respondent No.2, and if NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB there is any liability on their part, it should be indemnified by respondent No.2 and therefore, requested the dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Respondent No.2 contested the claim, stating that they were not the insurer of the lorry with registration No. KA-20/5937 at the time of the accident.
They also argued that the compensation sought by the petitioner is excessive.

Additionally, they claimed that the owner and insurer of the motorcycle should be considered necessary parties to the case, and the absence of these parties,
renders the petition legally flawed.

Respondent No.2 further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the motorcycle rider and that the lorry driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.
Consequently, they requested the dismissal of appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, the Tribunal framed the following issues for its consideration:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 10th July, 2015 at about 8.00pm, when he with one Shivraj was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-29/U-4591 on Bagalkot- NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB Kaladgi PWD Road, ridden by him, when opposite to Spinning Mill, he met with an accident and sustained injuries due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of lorry bearing Registration No.KA-29/5937?
2. Whether the respondent No.1 proves that he is not liable to pay compensation?
3. whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation sought for? If so, from whom?
4. What order or award?
8.
In order to prove their case, the petitioner got himself examined as PW1 and two doctors as PWs2 and 3 and got marked 17 documents as Exhibits P1 to P17.
On the other hand respondents have neither adduced any oral evidence nor produced documentary evidence.

sentences.text: In view of the above finding, Tribunal allowed the petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.19,90,200/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.

11. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the Tribunal committed an error in coming to the conclusion that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.
Learned counsel further submits that Tribunal has erred in considering the disability at 85% on the basis of the evidence of Doctor.
He also submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side, so also the awarding of interest at the rate of 9% is also on the higher side and needs to be revisited.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

12. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-claimant supported the impugned judgment and award and submits that considering the oral and documentary evidence NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB on record, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation and the same does not call for interference in this appeal.
Hence, he sought to dismiss the appeal.
13. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of record, the following points arise for our consideration in this appeal?
1. Whether the appellant-Insurance company has made out a ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and award?
2. What order?
14. The occurrence of accident is not in dispute, and it is also undisputed that the claimant sustained injuries as a result of the accident.

Regarding the liability of the appellant (the lorry owner), PW1 has provided clear testimony that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Registration No. KA-20/5937 by its driver.

Additionally, exhibits P1 to P3, which include the First Information Report, Complaint, and Charge sheet, confirm that a case was registered against the lorry driver for offenses punishable under Sections 279, 337, and 338 of the Indian Penal Code.
Exhibit P6, the wound certificate, provides NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB details of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Furthermore, nothing substantial was revealed during the cross-examination of PW1 to cast doubt on this evidence.
The order sheet of CC No.1723 of 2015 in the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Bagalkot, also indicates that the lorry driver admitted guilt for the alleged offence and paid a fine of Rs.1,700/-.

sentences.text: In addition to the above, without attributing any reasons, the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum on the compensation awarded by it.

Considering the fact that the rate of interest on the term and fixed deposits in the nationalised Banks in these years are reducing, the awarding of interest at the rate of 9% per annum is also on the higher side and thus the same is required to be reduced and re-fixed at 6% per annum.
The interference in the impugned judgment and award is warranted.
Barring the above, the appellant/Insurance Company has not raised any other ground worth to be considered and no arguments on any other point were also canvassed from the appellant's side.

In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER 1. Appeal partly allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8929-DB 2.
The rate of interest ordered by the Tribunal at the rate of 9% per annum also stands modified and fixed at 6% per annum, from the date of the claim petition till the date of payment;
